description: Transvaalbuurt 1929 portiek blocks of Tugelaweg 91-120: 14 m stair blocks of a dark purple-brown brick ground storey (2.4 m of dark brick) under three cream-rendered storeys and a flat roof run out as a deep white eaves slab; one grey rendered stair panel about 1.9 m wide over the portiek door on the block's middle axis, a small stair light per storey in it; either side a narrow window, a 1.6 m window with a small iron balcony on storeys 1-3, and at both ends half of a wide band window that the neighbour completes across the party wall

match.note: BAG 1929 on both Tugelaweg faces (91-112, 113-120); every stair block 14.0-15.0 m, 3DBAG eaves 12.9-13.0 m and bouwlagen 5 (the eaves slab counts), roof max 17.2-18.3 m (roof plant and stair heads, not a pitched roof). The cream render reads stucco on the 2020-04-29 strip (wall #b2a98f-#bbb39c raw), which no brick 1928-1931 block of the buurt does (Schalk Burgerstraat 45-131, Afrikanerplein 1-55, Albert Luthulistraat 6-32 are brick): stucco and wall are the criteria that keep the type off them. The end pands 91-92 (15.7 m, eaves 9.9 m: the three-storey corner wing) and 119-120 (eaves 9.9 m) fall outside the storey count and stay with the city tier. Axis pitch 1.2-5.0 m: the strip's window columns read 3 on the 14 m blocks (measureFacade groups each band window with its narrow neighbour; 95-96 reads 3 columns = 4.66 m).

flat-overhang.note: Tugelaweg 95-96 (075050): the flat roof's white eaves slab 13.0-13.4 m, grey soffit, about 0.9 m out (seen end-on over the corner wing of 91-92)

portiek.note: the portiek door (red-brown timber, 1.0 m) under the grey panel, a dark brick hood over it at 3.6-4.0 m; mailboxes either side

roof.evidence: strip 2020-04-29: sky directly over the eaves slab along the whole of 93-118; no roof face shows from the street (3DBAG roof max 17.2-18.3 m reads roof plant and a set-back roof behind)

rhythm.bays: half band window, balcony window, narrow window, stair panel, narrow window, balcony window, half band window
rhythm.identicalBays: no: the end band windows straddle the party walls, the stair axis a small light
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: windows + portiek door | 1-3: band window (shared) + balcony window + narrow window + stair light + narrow window + balcony window + band window (shared)
rhythm.groundFloor: dark brick, the portiek door under the stair panel, band windows either side
rhythm.roofline: flat, a deep white eaves slab

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2020-04-29 at 40 px/m, 1 m grid on 95-96 (075050, 13.9 m): dark brick to 4.0 m, ground windows 1.7-3.4 m; window rows 5.0-6.35, 7.8-9.05, 10.6-11.95 m (2.8 m pitch); eaves slab 13.0-13.4 m; grey panel 2.0 m wide on the stair axis from 4.0 m to the slab; band windows 3.0-3.1 m, narrow windows 1.1-1.3 m, balcony doors with iron balconies at the block ends (balcony pairs at the party walls of 93-94/95-96 and 95-96/97-98). Cream #b8b097, panel #9a9b94, brick #403d3c raw (fascia #dde4dd: x1/0.9 for the type palette)
strip.jpg 2020-04-29: the same block on 113-118, grey stair panels at a 14 m pitch

strip.jpg 2020-04-29, 1 m grid on 105-106 (14.0 m): stair panel 5.3-7.2 m, narrow windows 4.1-5.1 and 7.2-7.7 m, 1.5-2 m windows with small projecting iron balconies (0.6-1 m rails) on storeys 1-3 at 1.1-2.6 and 9.2-11.0 m, slit lights at 0.4 and 11.3 m, wide windows at 12.3-14 m and 0-0.5 m running across the party walls

strip.jpg 2020-04-29 at 40 px/m, heights over the facade foot (0.6 m on the strip): dark brick to 2.4 m, ground windows 1.1-2.3 m, window rows 3.6-5.0, 6.4-7.6, 9.0-10.0 m, the eaves slab's foot at 11.1 m; storeys 2.9 / 2.8 / 2.7 / 2.7 m (the first sheet drew the 4.1 m ground storey read on 95-96 without its foot offset: 1.8 m on that strip)

schemaLimits: the stair panel's paired slit lights per half landing are drawn as one small light per storey on the stair axis
the band windows' top-light rows of small panes and the slit lights beside the balcony windows are not drawn
the dark brick ground storey is a dark paint facing over the render (plaster grain, not brick; its orange header specks are not drawn)
BAG cuts the row so that the stair panel sits up to 1.8 m off the pand centre on some blocks (95-96 at 5.2 m of 13.9 m); the type draws it centred

the small iron balconies (0.3 m out) are drawn as flush guards, and the narrow windows either side of the stair panel without their top light: with both the stair block is 3,446 triangles against the 3,000 budget (flush guards 3,086, plain narrow windows 2,894)
notes: Kit (2026-11-01, #153): paintedStoreys.panels (fit.ts paintedPanelBlocks) draws the grey stair panel; the wall is the cream render (palette wallMaterial stucco) and the dark ground storey is paintedStoreys [0], one cut facing instead of three: the three painted upper storeys cost 790 triangles and put the stair block over the 3,000-triangle budget.

Roof: flat from the front (source front, form flat). The 3DBAG roof drew a 3-4 m red roof face over the slab that the strip never shows (tugelaweg-113-120-r1 sheet, 2026-11-01); only the end of the corner wing shows a roof face rising far behind.
Palette: the cream is the raw strip reading #b8b097 (the trim-normalised #cdc4a8 drew the stucco wall dL +0.16 lighter than the photo on 101-102 and 105-106).

Status 2026-11-01 (#153): with the measured storeys every Tugelaweg pand is held by the likeness gate (edge NCC 0.07-0.13). The strips put the facade foot 0.6-1.8 m over the strip ground and the eaves slab's foot 11.1 m over that, while 3DBAG draws the eaves at 12.9 m, so the model's storey lines sit 1-2 m off the photo's. Tugelaweg 113-116 passed the gate and was installed earlier the same day with a 4.1 m ground storey (the 95-96 reading taken without its foot offset) and was uninstalled once the strip-over-model sheet showed the error. The next step is the eaves height: read the front eaves off the strip (match.frontEavesM, as the 1923 types do) or a strip foot-offset fix in intake. Do not raise the gate.
